DCI.text: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 38.5% to ₹212 cr and profit 23% to ₹6.2 cr, led by IT products (+40%) and security software (+29%). The Oct–Dec quarter is the festive and year-end buying season for IT hardware, so revenue momentum should continue. But profit is likely to grow slower than sales: net margin is thin (2.9%), interest cost jumped 172%, borrowings rose to ₹123 cr, inventory is up and operating cash flow was −₹35 cr in H1. Watch whether interest costs stop rising. Expect strong sales growth with modest profit growth.

MODIS.text: H1 FY27 revenue rose 53% to ₹128 cr and profit 59% to ₹19 cr, with EBITDA margin up to 20.5%. Bookings jumped to ₹202 cr from ₹54 cr a year ago. ₹156 cr of already-sold flats is still to be booked as revenue, and two projects are well advanced: Rashmi Square (80% built) and Rashmi Signature (62%). Their revenue is recognised as construction progresses, which should keep the next quarters strong. Risks: real-estate revenue is lumpy, and two big projects (Icon, Avenue) are early-stage. Interest cost also appeared (₹1.2 cr) despite the company calling itself debt-free.

PANACHE.text: Q2 FY27 revenue more than doubled (+109%) to ₹82 cr and profit tripled (+220%) to ₹4.7 cr. The clearest next-quarter catalyst is a ₹51.4 cr laptop supply order from an IT-sector customer, announced on 2 Nov 2026 and due within about 30 days. That one order is over 60% of last quarter's sales and falls fully in Oct–Dec, so Q3 revenue growth looks very likely. Risks: the business is order-driven and lumpy, margins are thin (about 6% net), the customer is not named, and the share price already reflects much of the growth.

526433.text: Sales jumped to ₹268 cr in the Sep 2026 quarter (+74% YoY) and profit to ₹34 cr (+79%), up from ₹199 cr and ₹27 cr in June: strong and still rising. ASM provides engineering and product R&D services for overseas clients. Q3 is compared with a weak Dec 2025 quarter (₹116 cr sales, ₹9 cr profit), so even a flat quarter from here would mean very high YoY growth. The board declared a ₹6 interim dividend. Watch: promoter holding fell from 57.4% to 53.5% in October, and the stock trades at about 26× book value.

530477.text: Steady grower: Sep 2026 quarter sales ₹44 cr (+26% YoY) and profit ₹13.6 cr (+24%), the best quarter in the last five. Vikram Thermo makes pharma excipients (co-polymers used in tablet coatings and formulations) for domestic and export customers, a business with stable demand. Q3 is compared with Dec 2025 (₹34 cr sales, ₹11 cr profit), so holding the current run-rate would give about 25% growth. No new capacity or big orders have been announced, so growth depends on volumes continuing. Margins are high (about 30% net) and have held steady.

544406.text: H1 FY27 revenue rose 50% to ₹223 cr and profit 63% to ₹28 cr. Cash flow turned positive (+₹33 cr), receivables fell sharply and the company has no debt. It added more than 10 large enterprise clients, including Sun Pharma, Jio 5G, IDBI Bank, Kotak Bank and IDFC First Bank, plus a ₹27 cr cybersecurity order. Oct–Dec is usually a strong quarter for IT-infrastructure spending by banks, which bring 56% of its revenue. Risks: dependence on bank budgets, margins lower than in H2 FY26, and no order-book number disclosed.

ARIES.text: June 2026 quarter sales rose 17% to ₹188 cr and profit 50% to ₹15 cr, recovering from a loss in Mar 2026. Aries Agro sells specialty plant nutrients (chelated micronutrients, 134 brands), so results follow the crop seasons. Oct–Dec covers rabi sowing, and last year's Dec quarter was ₹202 cr sales and ₹17 cr profit. The Sep 2026 results come on 13 Nov 2026 and will show how kharif demand went, the best clue for Q3. Risks: weather-driven demand, margin swings (as in the Mar 2026 loss) and slow government subsidy payments.

AVTNPL.text: Five quarters of rising sales and profit: from ₹132 cr and ₹12 cr (Jun 2025) to ₹241 cr and ₹31 cr (Jun 2026). AVT (A.V. Thomas Group) makes plant-based extracts and natural ingredients for food, beverage, animal-nutrition and nutraceutical companies, much of it exported. If the current run-rate holds, Q3 sales would be about 25% above Dec 2025 (₹194 cr) and profit well above ₹17 cr. The Sep 2026 results come on 11 Nov 2026 and will confirm the trend. Risks: crop and raw-material prices, currency swings and customer concentration in exports.
